newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania has portfolio tax, application distant.
newsitem.headline: Romania has portfolio tax, application distant.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Tuesday it had approved a 1.5 percent tax on portfolio deals and brokers hoped the announcement would end confusion over procedures in the market.

A central bank spokesman said the taxation rate was set at the maximum 1.5 percent for six months as suggested by the government's Economic Reform Council. But officials at the Council said further procedural hurdles had to be cleared before the measure could come into force.

The government last month issued a decree introducing portfolio investment rules for the first time and amending and complementing a 1991 foreign investment law. It said norms for its application would be issued within a month.

Portfolio rules said repatriation of initial investment and capital gains was free and set a tax of up to 1.5 percent on each deal. The tax rate was to be set by the Economic Reform Council and the BNR on a six-month basis.
"With the BNR approval in our hands we'll send it to market regulator CNVM," a Council official said. "It will look into it and give it to brokers for application."
Brokers said confusion in the market stemmed from when and how the new tax was to be applied.
"Some brokers already charged the tax on request by clients who want to have capital gains repatriation guaranteed," said Creditanstalt Securities president Marcel Cobuz.
"There was great confusion with some brokers charging the tax on the day of the deal and others on settlement day," a securities dealer said.
Some brokerage houses applied the tax to the overall value of the deal, including their commission. Clients complained, saying that meant paying twice, he added.
The Council official said the tax was to be charged on settlement day, applied to the total worth of traded shares.
"The tax would be applied the day the buyer becomes owner of the shares and the broker's commission should not be included in the value of the deal," he said.

Portfolio investors entered Romania's equities market only this year after pledges by the centrist government elected last November to fight corruption and encourage foreign investment and capital market growth.
Their presence has significantly increased volumes traded on both the stock exchange and the over-the-counter market.
